findings.description: Critical: The Git-based staleness rule does not define what happens when the last commit timestamp is later than the host manifest as_of. Git permits future-dated commits, so the specified subtraction can produce a negative staleness_days (rejected by digest.schema.json) or, if fed directly into the formula, a negative penalty that incorrectly boosts the candidate.
findings.resolution: Specify and test a fail-closed clock-skew rule: when commit_time > as_of, emit staleness_days: null plus an explicit degraded marker (or clamp to zero, if that is the intended policy), and never allow a negative value into the formula.

findings.description: Critical: Lifecycle maintenance is required to delete terminal stub/cache files and publish a rebuilt digest as one maintained baseline, but the recovery journal is defined only in terms of replacement bytes/checksums for cache, digest, and mirror targets. It neither represents deletions nor explicitly includes candidate-store removal. A crash after pruning and before the digest/mirror replacements can therefore leave durable mixed state that the stated roll-forward protocol cannot reconstruct.
findings.resolution: Extend the transaction contract to encode both replace and delete operations, include terminal stub/cache deletions and the rebuilt mirror/digest in the same journal, define per-parent-directory fsync and digest-last ordering, and add interruption tests for every deletion/replacement boundary during terminal-only and mixed prune/wake maintenance.

findings.description: Revision 4 correctly separates generated_at from state_updated_at, allowing lifecycle-only rebuilds to preserve cache evidence time while exposing the later state transition.
findings.resolution: Preserve this two-clock contract and its cache-only validation tests during implementation.
